newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PARIS ST GERMAIN CRUSH LIVERPOOL 3-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARIS ST GERMAIN CRUSH LIVERPOOL 3-0.

text.p: Paris St Germain took a giant step towards their second consecutive European Cup Winners' Cup final when they crushed Liverpool 3-0 in their semifinal first leg at the Parc des Princes on Thursday.

The Parisians, bidding to become the first team to retain the trophy, took an early lead thanks to Brazilian Leonardo, who took advantage of a blunder by Liverpool goalkeeper David James in the 10th minute to score his first goal of 1997.
James was again to blame for PSG's second goal as he dropped the ball on a cross from the right to allow midfielder Benoit Cauet to make it 2-0 just before the break.
But there was nothing James could do to stop PSG's third goal, scored from close range by Jerome Leroy in the 83rd minute from a pass by substitute Cyrille Pouget.
Liverpool were defensively naive against the experienced Parisians, playing in their fifth consecutive European semifinal.
Leonardo was especially impressive, starting most of PSG's most dangerous moves.
France goalkeeper Bernard Lama was in much better form than his Liverpool counterpart and his goal was hardly ever in danger.
History shows Liverpool have always lost away to French teams in European cup competitions before qualifying at Anfield in the second leg.
But they will need an outstanding performance in two weeks to retain their hopes of lifting the only European trophy they have yet to win.
